newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies mixed, yen inside Monday's ranges.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies mixed, yen inside Monday's ranges.

text.p: IMM currency futures opened mixed, with key currencies trading inside of Monday's ranges in quiet activity.
There was little pit trade to report, aside from light trading in the yen futures pit and some selling of Canadian dollar futures, traders said.

Most mark contracts and Swiss franc futures softened, as the dollar corrected Monday's losses amid a lack of fresh news on the European monetary union (EMU). Traders and currency analysts appear to be split on whether a EMU budget stability pact will be signed at the June 16 meeting in Amsterdam.
"Amsterdam won't achieve anything," one currency market trader said about the European Union meeting on Monday.
The agenda at the EU meeting in Amsterdam includes an action plan and timetable covering all necessary measures that must be taken before beginning the next step towards EMU.
Uncertainties about a timely start to the euro heightened on Monday when France asked its EU partners for a period of consultation on the budget stability pact.
The new French government needed at least a week to consider the budget accord, the French finance minister said on Monday.
Cash mark's rise against most other European currencies, including the French franc, are expected to support mark futures and drag down dollar/mark in the near term.
One currency market source said talk circulated that the Bank of France would keep mark/Paris bound below 3.3850. A rally to 3.39 to 3.3950 would ignite mark buying, traders said.

However, September marks are expected to continue their long-term downtrend, as the dollar/mark is forecast to benefit from EMU jitters, they said. One analyst said September marks would have close above $0.6050 to turn their trend higher.
September yen were higher, but remained below Monday's pit high of $0.009037 and the GLOBEX high of $0.009060, which is also the contract's highest level in almost six months.
One analyst said yen futures were finding support on growing expectations that the U.S. administration may be ready to use the dollar as a trade tool.
Such expectations have been compounded by recent U.S. officials' comments ahead of the Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Denver on June 20-22, they said.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's reiteration that the U.S. favors a strong dollar calmed yen selling, they said.

One analyst expects September yen and marks to stabilize in the near term, as the dollar should find buyers on any probes below 111.00 spot yen, or $0.009136 September yen, and 1.70 spot marks, or $0.5924 September marks.

At 0812 CDT/1312 GMT, September yen was up $0.000037 at $0.009008, marks fell $0.0018 at $0.5880, Swiss francs were $0.0010 lower at $0.7023, sterling was up $0.0028 at $1.6348, Canadian dollars were up $0.0009 at $0.7264, Australian dollars were $0.0003 higher at $0.7628 and Mexican pesos were $0.000200 higher at $0.120050.
